title: Homogeneous polynomial evaluation and inhomogeneous normalization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$. Put $A(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on the coherent profinite site [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ for $r\geq0$, with its product topology [def-sfb-ladic-lattice]. Use internal $A$-modules and internal $L$-actions [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module], in coefficient universes containing the site and every profinite parameter set [def-weil-size-convention].

For $n\geq0$, let $K^n$ be the internal direct sum of copies of $A$ on the monomials in the $(n+1)r$ variables $y_0,\ldots,y_n$, each an $r$-tuple [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Give it the diagonal action $(g\cdot f)(y_0,\ldots,y_n)=f(y_0-g,\ldots,y_n-g)$, for every section $g\in C(S,L)$, and the differential
$$(\delta f)(y_0,\ldots,y_{n+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^if(y_0,\ldots,\widehat y_i,\ldots,y_{n+1}).$$
Set $K^n=0$ for $n<0$, and let $a:A[0]\to K$ include the constants, with trivial action on $A$.

Let $P^n$ be the internal polynomial direct sum on the $nr$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, each an $r$-tuple, zero in negative degrees, with differential
$$(dp)(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1})=p(x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^ip(x_1,\ldots,x_i+x_{i+1},\ldots,x_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}p(x_1,\ldots,x_n).$$

Use the internal homogeneous function module [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions]
$$R_A^n=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline L^{n+1}],A),$$
with diagonal translation of its arguments, alternating deletion differential and constant augmentation $b:A[0]\to R_A^\bullet$, and put $U_A^n=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline L^n],A)$ with the inhomogeneous bar faces [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. There is an internal $A$-linear equivariant cochain map $e:K\to R_A^\bullet$, with $ea=b$, specified on every monomial $y^m$ and every section coefficient $c\in A(S)$ by
$$e^n(cy^m)(s,g_0,\ldots,g_n)=c(s)\prod_{a=0}^n\prod_{i=1}^r(g_a)_i^{m_{a,i}}.$$
This specification holds after every profinite base change $T\to S$ as well, restricting $c$ and allowing every tuple $g_a\in C(T,L)$. Via $\phi(p)(y)=p(y_1-y_0,\ldots,y_n-y_{n-1})$ and the invariant homogeneous-function identification obtained by evaluating at $(0,g_1,g_1+g_2,\ldots,g_1+\cdots+g_n)$, the induced cochain map $P\to U_A^\bullet$ is exactly polynomial evaluation:
$$c\prod_{a,i}x_{a,i}^{m_{a,i}}\longmapsto\bigl[(s,g_1,\ldots,g_n)\mapsto c(s)\prod_{a,i}(g_a)_i^{m_{a,i}}\bigr].$$
For $n=0$ and for $r=0$ the empty products are $1$, and the degree-zero augmentation is the given constant inclusion. These are maps with all continuous $F$-valued coefficients, including noncomplete $\Omega$, without any assertion about higher acyclicity of $R_A^n$ or $U_A^n$.

proof.text: All formulas can be interpreted internally. On a polynomial monomial, a translation or a deletion gives a finite polynomial expansion, with coefficients in the section ring; restriction preserves its additions and products. The polynomial universal property therefore gives the substitutions and their identities. Extend the maps from the summands by the universal property of the internal direct sum. On functions, use precomposition on every slice family. Two successive deletions of positions $i<j$ occur in the two orders with signs $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$, so they cancel. This proves $\delta^2=0$ for both homogeneous complexes. Deletion commutes with simultaneous translation, and the differences of the two constant faces cancel on constants. Thus the displayed homogeneous differentials and augmentations have the stated actions and are cochain maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-image input; agent argument: well-defined homogeneous complexes

proof.text: For each monomial $y^m$, define a section of $R_A^n$ over the terminal profinite object by its slice evaluations $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)\in C(T,L)^{n+1}\mapsto\prod_{a,i}(x_a)_i^{m_{a,i}}\in C(T,F)$. The embedding $\mathbf Z_\ell\to F$ preserves the restricted norm, hence is continuous. Every coordinate, finite power and finite product in this formula is continuous. The formula commutes with every $T'\to T$, since pullback is composition and preserves pointwise products. The internal-function description in def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data therefore makes this a genuine section, not merely a function on global points. Multiplication by it gives an internal $A$-linear map from the monomial summand $A$ to $R_A^n$. The coproduct universal property gives $e^n:K^n\to R_A^n$. Its value on $cy^m$ on the slice $T\xrightarrow{f}S$ is $(f^*c)\prod_{a,i}(x_a)_i^{m_{a,i}}$. This proves the stated formula and all its base changes. The construction by summands also covers sections that are only locally finite sums, without imposing a global support bound.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-image input; agent argument: construction of evaluation on the internal polynomial direct sum

proof.text: Let $g\in C(S,L)$ and $x_a\in C(T,L)$ over $f:T\to S$. Polynomial substitution and evaluation give $e^n(g\cdot q)_f(x)=e^n(q)_f(x_0-f^*g,\ldots,x_n-f^*g)$. Indeed, both sides are the homomorphism evaluating each variable $y_{a,i}$ at $(x_a)_i-(f^*g)_i$, with the same restricted coefficients. The normalized homogeneous-function action has exactly this formula because $A$ has trivial $L$-action. Hence $e^n(g\cdot q)=g\cdot e^n(q)$ after every base change, which is equivariance in the specified action category.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-image input; agent argument: equivariance of evaluation

proof.text: For every tuple $(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+1})$ on every slice, evaluating a polynomial after omitting $y_i$ is evaluating the original polynomial on $(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{n+1})$: the two evaluation homomorphisms agree on coefficients and variables. Taking the same alternating sum on both sides yields $e^{n+1}\delta=\delta e^n$. The family description of internal functions makes equality of all these evaluations equality of internal maps. Constants evaluate to the same constants, so $e^0a=b$ in degree zero and $ea=b$ as augmented cochain maps. Set $e^n=0$ in negative degrees.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-image input; agent argument: cochain and augmentation identities

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-homogeneous-polynomial-invariant-coordinates with the very same $\ell,F,L,A$ and polynomial direct sums. Its fixed-section convention includes every profinite base change, exactly as here. It supplies the cochain isomorphism $\phi:P^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}(K^\bullet)^L$ by consecutive differences, with inverse given by prefix sums starting at zero. In particular it supplies that the displayed $P$ differential squares to zero. Equivariance from step 3 lets $e$ restrict to a cochain map on these invariant submodules.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-image input; agent argument: the already-existing polynomial invariant-coordinate isomorphism

proof.text: Write $\chi_n$ for prefix evaluation on invariant homogeneous internal functions. To check it is the asserted identification, define its inverse on a slice family $c$ by $\psi_n(c)(h_0,\ldots,h_n)=c(h_1-h_0,\ldots,h_n-h_{n-1})$. Prefix sums and differences are continuous maps of the profinite powers of $L$, so precomposing the natural families defines internal $A$-linear maps and commutes with every base change. The function $\psi_n(c)$ is fixed under simultaneous translation since each difference is unchanged. Conversely, a fully fixed homogeneous function $H$ satisfies $H(h_0,\ldots,h_n)=H(0,h_1-h_0,\ldots,h_n-h_0)$: apply invariance with translating section $h_0$ on that slice. Successive differences of $(0,g_1,g_1+g_2,\ldots,g_1+\cdots+g_n)$ are $(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$; its prefix reconstruction from the differences of $h$ is $(0,h_1-h_0,\ldots,h_n-h_0)$. Thus $\chi_n\psi_n=1$ and $\psi_n\chi_n=1$ on all slice evaluations.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-image input; agent argument: internal homogeneous-function invariant coordinates

proof.text: Put $t_0=0$ and $t_j=g_1+\cdots+g_j$. In $(\chi_{n+1}\delta H)(g)$, deletion of $t_0$ gives $H(t_1,\ldots,t_{n+1})=H(0,g_2,g_2+g_3,\ldots,g_2+\cdots+g_{n+1})$, by translating by $t_1=g_1$. Deletion of $t_i$ for $1\leq i\leq n$ changes precisely the adjacent differences $g_i,g_{i+1}$ into $g_i+g_{i+1}$; deletion of $t_{n+1}$ drops $g_{n+1}$. With the unchanged signs $(-1)^i$, these are exactly the first, interior and last terms of the displayed inhomogeneous differential. This proves $\chi_{n+1}\delta=d\chi_n$ on every slice. For $n=0$, it says $H(g_1)-H(0)=0$, agreeing with $dc=c-c=0$ for trivial coefficients. Hence $\chi$ is a cochain isomorphism, and $\rho=\chi\circ e^L\circ\phi$ is the induced cochain map $P\to U_A^\bullet$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-image input; agent argument: face-by-face differential identification

proof.text: For a monomial $p=c\prod_{a,i}x_{a,i}^{m_{a,i}}$, steps 2 and 5 give $\rho^n(p)(g)=c\prod_{a,i}(t_a-t_{a-1})_i^{m_{a,i}}=c\prod_{a,i}(g_a)_i^{m_{a,i}}$, on every profinite slice, since $t_a-t_{a-1}=g_a$. This is exactly the required polynomial evaluation map. In degree zero there are no difference variables, $\phi(c)$ is constant and $\chi_0e^0\phi(c)=c$; thus the augmentation is the specified constant inclusion. For $r=0$, every $L$-power is terminal and every term is $A$, all substitutions and evaluations are identities, and the unnormalized differential is multiplication by $\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i$ on both sides. No step used an infinite sum, a limit in $F$, or completeness: all continuous $\Omega$-valued coefficients remain allowed.
